messages:
sam: Following up on the migration RFC  idea: build a tiny compatibility proxy that normalizes old request envelopes to the new streaming contract. Gate it per-tenant. Keep transformations minimal and avoid re-encoding token blobs.
nora: Agree on minimalism. Big risk is buffering. If we wait for full message before emitting we'll break low-latency clients. Need pass-through when possible.
henry: Implementation sketch: sniff first byte/frame, if already v3, route directly; if legacy, rewrite only headers and wrap chunk bytes in a single envelope without touching content. No decode/encode.
ci_bot: CI: compat-proxy unit tests queued -> run 12m :gear:
sre_bot: Operational constraints: add a circuit-breaker that fails open to `429` with `Retry-After` and header `X-RI-Compat: degraded` if proxy p95 > 275ms for 5m OR error_rate > 1%. Also tag traces with `compat.proxy=true`.
sam: Also require explicit tenant opt-in via header `X-RI-Compat: enable=v1`. Default OFF. Rollout timeline proposal: 2w opt-in canary -> 2w warning opt-out -> then enforce after customer notice (max 180d lifetime).
nora: Telemetry plan: counters `compat.requests`, `compat.passthrough`, `compat.rewrites`, histograms for latency. Dashboard and alert thresholds needed before canary.
henry: Tests: replay recorded streams including out-of-order and partial-chunk cases. Integration: 0.5% production traffic canary comparing token-by-token output vs native path for standard prompts.
sam: I'll write rollout checklist and owners. henry/nora own tests and dashboards. If no objections I'll start canary next Monday. :shipit:
nora: fine with me.
sre_bot: On-call ready for canary window.
